Staged-vs-committed hash: when a mode 1 (granted) STAGE_GENERATION on the initiator fails with -EPERM (stale/unknown parent), fall back AT ONCE to a fresh (mode 0) attempt, forget the stored session hash, and log a specific line saying the parent was refused; respect the normal backoff so there is no storm. On the responder side, if staging a mode 1 INIT fails with -EPERM, log a specific line (it cannot answer; the initiator's attempt window will time out and fall back). Verify against kernel/runtime/gateway.c and docs/AY4_ACTIVATION.md what errno the kernel really returns before coding.
2. Lost REKEY_GRANTED: the kernel sends the event once. Before falling back to a flow-clearing fresh attempt after GRANT_WAIT, the controller should repeat REKEY_REQUEST for the same attempt on a short schedule inside the wait (e.g. 1 s, 2 s) IF the kernel accepts a repeated REKEY_REQUEST for the same attempt (check gateway.c / netlink.c and AY4_ACTIVATION.md: the responder side is documented idempotent; check the initiator side). If the kernel does not accept repeats, do not change behaviour and instead document the gap precisely in docs/CONTROLLER.md 'Not covered'.
3. Pending deadline: tie the attempt/grant deadline to the kernel's windows (they start at BEGIN_ATTEMPT / REKEY_REQUEST, not when the INIT leaves) if this is a small change; otherwise document it.
4. Tests (add to session.rs / adversarial.rs where the existing TestPort allows; extend the fake with scripted errors): a stage returning -EPERM in mode 1 triggers an immediate fresh fallback; the literal 5 s grant wait pinned with literals instead of the GRANT_WAIT constant; `a_stale_or_foreign_grant_does_nothing` must assert state after the 'nothing waiting' case; parse_rekey_event for truncated/wrong-size/unknown-command input (error, not panic); the rekey_request and stage_generation encoders (byte layout); on_rekey_needed returning true/false cases; session_hash survives a reconfigure for a kept peer and is cleared for a replaced one; a wrong-but-self-consistent parent is caught by comparing to the first session's real hash. For each new test of a behaviour you changed, prove with one temporary mutation that it fails, then restore.
5. Fix the stale comments the review lists (session.rs top-of-file comment, exchange.rs ~355, daemon.rs ~303-305 about lost events, CONTROLLER.md/AY4_REKEY.md table lines that contradict the code) and add the A43 operator note to docs/CONTROLLER.md and docs/DEMO.md: a gateway must not be suspended, snapshotted or cloned while running (the kernel measures lease and key age on the boot clock, so time passed during suspend counts and sessions expire; a restored snapshot repeats nonce/sequence state), keep it short and factual, say what is verified (unit test injecting a suspend-sized clock jump) and what is not (a real suspend).

Then report `gh pr checks` state (wait at most ~5 minutes) and per finding: fixed / documented only / skipped, with reasons. Also state precisely if PR #72 (branch raj/drop-counter-liveness) is merged yet and whether your branch conflicts with it.

Review of the controller half of PR #71 (commit 4df579f "AY4 controller: granted re-key..." plus the liveness consumer that came in with the merge, b51e481). I own control/ and had not read this part before. This is a reading review at origin/main 29f7831. I did not run the Rust tests, the C unit tests, the netns scripts or any VM, so every statement below about behaviour is from reading the code and docs, and "caught by test X" means "an assertion in X would fail on paper", not that I mutated and ran it.

All line numbers are at 29f7831.

## What I checked and found right

* Ordering. start_attempt (control/src/session.rs:463) calls BEGIN_ATTEMPT first (:465), then REKEY_REQUEST with the attempt it got (:474), parks in AwaitGrant (:476-481), and only on a matching REKEY_GRANTED does on_rekey_granted (:365-391) send the mode 1 INIT with the parent. The kernel requires exactly this order: rekey_request wants a live, not-yet-done attempt with the same ID (kernel/runtime/gateway.c:2298), and the initiator locator reused in the INIT is the one BEGIN_ATTEMPT issued (STAGE checks it, netlink.c:154).
* Late, repeated or foreign grants are ignored: wrong state returns at :375-377, wrong attempt at :378-380. A duplicate GRANTED cannot start a second INIT because the first one moves the state to Pending.
* Responder side does check the parent. respond() refuses a mode 1 INIT unless params.continuity_grant == Some(got.parent) (control/src/exchange.rs:414), and session.rs:651 feeds it the peer's session_hash. The RESPONSE echoes the parent and the initiator checks it (exchange.rs:328). The kernel is the real gate (gateway.c:2200-2216: parent must equal the current generation hash AND a live, unused grant for exactly this attempt must exist, else -EPERM).
* No concurrent double start. Both request_rekey (:338) and on_rekey_needed (:351) only act on Established and only set a bool; start_attempt clears it (:464). Any trigger that arrives while the peer is AwaitGrant, Pending or Idle is dropped, and that is safe because each of those states already ends in a new attempt.
* Reconfigure: kept peers keep everything (state including AwaitGrant, session_hash, rekey_requested, cached), which is right because the kernel keeps the peer object when the incarnation is unchanged. Replaced and added peers get Idle, session_hash None (:449), so the next attempt is fresh. That is right: a new kernel peer has no session to continue. Events for a removed or replaced slot find no matching state and fall out (on_rekey_granted :372-374, on_rekey_needed :359).
* parse_rekey_event (control/src/vptunnel.rs:212) cannot panic on any input I could construct: get(4..) instead of indexing, attributes() returns errors, the slot and incarnation conversions are try_from. A malformed event is logged and ignored (daemon.rs:294).
* No storm from the fallback. GrantTimeout (:309-316) and a refused REKEY_REQUEST (:484-491) start one fresh attempt per trigger and nothing re-arms them; that fresh attempt has the normal 10 s deadline and, on failure, the normal 1,2,4,8,16,30 backoff (:318-331).

## Findings, most important first

1. The controller's session_hash is the hash of the last STAGED generation, not of the generation the kernel has COMMITTED, and the controller gets no signal about activation. (session.rs:676, :705; "Established" is set at stage time, :675, :704; CONTROLLER.md:175 even says so.) In the normal case activation completes in milliseconds and the two agree. When activation does not complete (candidate dropped after 10 s with ACTIVATION_FAILED, gateway.c act_work_fn 1218+), both controllers believe H1 while both kernels still have H0 as current. The next age-timer re-key then goes: REKEY_REQUEST succeeds, REKEY_START carries the kernel's H0 and the responder grants it, GRANTED arrives, the controller sends a mode 1 INIT with parent H1. The responder's controller accepts it (its session_hash is also H1), but its STAGE says parent H1 is not the current hash H0 and the kernel answers -EPERM. The responder prints "cannot install keys" and sends no RESPONSE (:664-667); the initiator retransmits for 10 s, expires, backs off 1 s and only then makes a fresh attempt. So the stale-parent case does recover, but it costs about 11 s plus the 5 s grant window of the previous step, and it ends in the flow-clearing fresh path, with the only trace being a generic log line. The same root cause explains a second, lesser case: if the kernel's soft-limit REKEY_NEEDED fires again 5 s later while a slow activation is still pending, the controller is "Established" and starts another granted re-key against the wrong parent. Suggested fix (small): on a stage failure of a Rekey-mode attempt, or on -EPERM in particular, log it as "continuity refused" and fall back at once to a fresh attempt without waiting for expiry; better, have the kernel raise an event when a candidate commits or fails so the controller sets session_hash and Established from the commit. I would at least document in AY4_ACTIVATION.md that session_hash is the staged hash.

2. A lost REKEY_GRANTED event costs the flows, and the daemon message says the opposite. daemon.rs:303-306 logs "waiting for retransmission" when the inbox reports loss, and the comment says a lost event heals itself. That is true for INIT/RESPONSE (they are retransmitted) but not for REKEY_GRANTED: the kernel sends it once (gateway.c:1174-1186, rk_state becomes RK_GRANTED and stays), and netlink.c:614 says "the controller's own timers recover". The controller's timer is GRANT_WAIT, which ends in a fresh attempt (:309-316) that clears the flows, even though the kernel grant is still live for another 5 s. The inbox's own doc (genl/inbox.rs top comment) says a lost event should lead to a resync. A cheap fix is to repeat REKEY_REQUEST for the same attempt when events were lost while a peer is in AwaitGrant: from my reading, the kernel resets rk_state to REQUESTED (gateway.c:2302-2307), the responder answers a repeat of the same attempt while its grant is live and unused (gateway.c:1146-1158), and the initiator raises GRANTED again. I did not run this. REKEY_NEEDED loss is benign: the kernel re-raises every 5 s while the soft limit persists, and the closure case is covered by the LIVENESS_LOST counter poll.

3. Two triggers for a closed peer can produce two re-keys, one right after the other. The kernel raises REKEY_NEEDED for first_loss (gateway.c:1357-1360) and bumps LIVENESS_LOST; the daemon also polls the counter once a second (daemon.rs:256-279) and calls request_rekey. The event is handled within about 100 ms, so the fresh attempt usually finishes before the next counter poll; the poll then sees the rise, the peer is Established again, and a second, granted re-key starts at once. It does no harm (the second one is mode 1 and keeps flows) but it is wasted work and it shows there is no minimum spacing in the controller: the only spacing is the kernel's 5 s limiter on NEEDED, the once-per-generation rule in usage::Monitor and the 15 s limiter in Silence. The responder-driven REKEY_NEEDED record (authenticated, one per 5 s) can also make the initiator do a granted re-key every 5 s. A guard in on_rekey_needed and request_rekey ("ignore if the session is younger than about 10 s", using Established.since) would remove both. This is a likely race from reading, not something I observed.

4. The Pending deadline is not anchored to the kernel's attempt and grant windows. send_init sets Pending.started = now at the time of the INIT (session.rs:544-549), but the kernel's attempt deadline is BEGIN_ATTEMPT + 10 s (gateway.c:2105, checked at stage with -ETIMEDOUT, :2127) and the initiator's grant deadline is REKEY_REQUEST + 10 s (:2300-2306). A grant that arrives after t seconds leaves only 10 - t seconds for the exchange, up to 5 s, while the controller keeps retransmitting for 10 s. A RESPONSE that arrives late then fails to stage; the initiator logs, waits 1 s (on_response error path, :710-716, which also does not bump failures) and goes fresh. Fix: carry Awaiting.started into Pending.started for a granted attempt. Low severity.

5. Fresh fallback semantics worth stating plainly (design, not defect). Any hiccup in the granted path ends in a flow-clearing fresh re-key and never in a second granted try: no grant in 5 s (:309), REKEY_REQUEST refused for any reason (:484), a granted INIT that expires (Expire then Idle then Start with granted=false, :286, :307), a stage error (:710). In all but the second the old session is still valid at that moment. That is acceptable, but it is why the "no packets lost" claim is conditional (see the EXPLANATION corrections). GrantTimeout is not counted in counts.attempts_failed and does not touch failures, so metrics and backoff do not see it; only the log line does. Also note the kernel keeps sending REKEY_START for the abandoned attempt until its own 10 s deadline (gateway.c:1268-1276), and the responder holds that grant for 10 s, so a REKEY_REQUEST in that window would not be granted (gateway.c:1161).

6. Tests: what is pinned and what is not (paper mutations).
   * a_rekey_asks_for_a_grant_and_the_granted_init_names_the_old_session (session.rs:1127): catches mode 0 instead of 1 on the granted INIT, a zero or missing parent (asserted non-zero, and the responder's controller would reject it), a stale parent on the third re-key (asserted different from the second), no REKEY_REQUEST call, and a REKEY_REQUEST with the wrong attempt (the fake would hand back that wrong attempt and no INIT would go). It does NOT catch a wrong but self-consistent parent, because the test only compares initiator parent with responder parent, which both come from the same INIT (exchange.rs:233); nothing compares it with the first session's real handshake hash. It would not notice if both sides used some other consistent 32 bytes.
   * without_a_grant_the_initiator_falls_back_to_a_fresh_attempt (:1156): catches "skip the wait" (it asserts staged.len() == 1 while withholding), fallback in mode 1 (asserts Fresh and zero parent), the >= boundary at exactly GRANT_WAIT, and a repeated REKEY_REQUEST (asserts one). It does not pin the value 5 s, because it advances by the constant GRANT_WAIT itself; changing it to 1 s or 60 s passes.
   * a_stale_or_foreign_grant_does_nothing (:1171): catches a missing attempt comparison. The comment says it also covers "a grant that arrives with nothing waiting", but the second call uses slot 9, which is unknown, and the test makes no assertion afterwards, so removing the AwaitGrant state check at :375-377 would pass. A grant arriving while Pending or Established, which is the case that would be dangerous (a second Initiator::start replacing the pending one), is untested. The positive case of on_rekey_needed (initiator, Established returns true) is also untested; only the unknown-slot and responder negatives are asserted. NEEDED in AwaitGrant, Pending, Idle is untested.
   * The fake port (:787-800) always delivers a grant if not withheld, never models the kernel's refusal of mode 1 without a grant, and never returns -EPERM from stage. So the stale-parent path (finding 1), a mode 1 INIT without a kernel grant and the stage-failure fallback have no test at all. adversarial.rs's fake kernel (:136-147) always refuses REKEY_REQUEST, so the whole adversarial suite exercises the fresh path only; none of the 37 tests runs the granted path under loss, forgery or reorder.
   * No unit tests exist for parse_rekey_event (vptunnel.rs:196-241), for the rekey_request builder (:182-194), or for stage_generation (:161-178) emitting PARENT_HASH only in mode 1. A mistake there (wrong attribute, missing parent) would only show up in ay4_activation.py, as a fresh fallback, and the script's check is a log-text grep ("making a fresh attempt" absent). That script, as written, does pin the happy path end to end (first session fresh, at least three granted INITs, grants counted in both kernels, 0 ping loss at 100 ms), but I did not run it. Nothing end to end exercises REKEY_NEEDED reaching the controller (no test greps "the kernel asked for a re-key"), GRANT_WAIT against a real kernel, or reconfigure during a granted re-key.
   * Reconfigure: a_policy_only_reload_keeps_the_session_and_its_timers (:1299) cannot tell whether session_hash was kept, because if it were reset the next re-key would silently become a fresh one and attempts_started would still go up by one. A mutation that resets session_hash or drops AwaitGrant on kept would pass.

7. Smaller points.
   * on_rekey_needed ignores the event's kernel_incarnation (daemon.rs:289 drops it with `..`), so a stale event for a replaced slot could cause one extra re-key if the new peer is Established by then. Compare it with peers[i].kernel_incarnation.
   * is_established (session.rs:243-247) counts AwaitGrant as established while request_rekey and on_rekey_needed require plain Established. Harmless but the doc comment "complete and still current" is only true because the old session is still current.
   * A responder that gets a mode 1 INIT with no kernel grant answers nothing and logs "cannot install keys" (:664-667); it is not counted as rejected, and each retransmit repeats the Noise work. This is the already documented limit at CONTROLLER.md:174, but a mode 1 INIT without a grant is now a reachable case and the -EPERM is not distinguished in the log.
   * Receive ordering of the new mechanism (kernel side, outside the controller): the initiator commits at READY and sends data under the new key; the responder keeps the candidate (data dropped, counted RX_CANDIDATE_DROPPED, datapath.c:508-512) until COMMIT arrives. If COMMIT is lost or overtaken, data is dropped until the 0.5 s retry. The tests ran on clean or 20 ms links. This is relevant to how strongly the docs say "no packets lost".

## Documentation and comment inconsistencies

* control/src/session.rs:15-18 still says re-keying is not hitless and the overlap "is AY4". Stale.
* control/src/exchange.rs:355 documents continuity_grant as "Parent hash of a live continuity grant from REKEY_START"; the controller now passes its own session_hash (session.rs:651), which is not a grant. Rename or re-document.
* control/src/daemon.rs:303-305, see finding 2.
* docs/CONTROLLER.md:209 still says "No REKEY_START continuity grant, no activation handshake (CONFIRM/READY/COMMIT)" and "INIT/RESPONSE are the only control messages the controller sends"; and lines 45-48, 59-65 do not mention the grant, the fresh fallback or REKEY_NEEDED. The sentence about LIVENESS_LOST is accurate but does not mention that the kernel's REKEY_NEEDED event now covers the same case per peer.
* docs/AY4_ACTIVATION.md is accurate on the points I could check against the code (5 s grant wait, immediate fresh when the grant cannot be asked, responder gets -EPERM on REKEY_REQUEST, rate limits). It does not say that the controller's "established" and parent are the staged ones (finding 1) or that a lost GRANTED event costs the flows (finding 2). Its "Not done" could carry both.
* docs/AY4_REKEY.md still has the table and the "next becomes current on the first authenticated record or after 2 seconds" text (lines on the next generation) with only a one-line "Superseded" note near the end, and still claims "no change to ... the controller". It will mislead a reader who stops at the table.
* docs/AY4_LIVENESS.md:6-8 says "does not change ... the controller" (true of that PR, not of main).

## What I would ask for before relying on this in the demo

(a) a test with a port that returns -EPERM on a Rekey-mode stage and shows the fallback; (b) a test that a GRANTED arriving while Pending or Established does nothing, using a known slot; (c) unit tests for parse_rekey_event (truncated, wrong command, missing attribute, slot over 255, NEEDED vs GRANTED); (d) a unit test that on_rekey_needed returns true for an Established initiator and false in AwaitGrant, Pending and Idle; (e) finding 1 either fixed or documented; (f) the daemon log line corrected. None of these needs a VM.

1:# Re-keying without losing packets (AY4)
2:
3:Every 90 seconds the controller runs a fresh Noise exchange and installs a new key generation, because a
4:generation lives at most 180 seconds. Before this change the kernel replaced the old generation at once, and
5:two things were lost: packets sent under the old keys that were still in flight, and packets one side sent
6:under new keys before the other side had them. With 20 ms of delay each way that was 10 of 2000 packets in
7:each direction over two re-keys.
8:
9:## What the kernel does now
10:
11:A peer holds up to three generations, each addressed by its own receive locator.
12:
13:| Generation | Sends | Receives | How it arrives and leaves |
14:|---|---|---|---|
15:| **current** | yes | yes | the one in use |
16:| **next** | no | yes | installed by `STAGE_GENERATION` while a current one exists |
17:| **prev** | no | yes, for 10 s | the replaced current, wiped by a delayed work after the grace |
18:
19:- The first generation of a peer, or one installed when the current one is past its hard age, becomes current at
20:  once. Nothing worth keeping is left.
21:- On a re-key the new generation becomes **next**. It receives immediately, so a record under the new keys is
22:  never refused. The peer keeps sending under the current generation.
23:- **next becomes current** on the first record that authenticates and passes replay under it (the other side
24:  switched), or when 2 seconds have passed, whichever is first. The old current becomes **prev**.
25:- Sending never uses next or prev, so a replaced key cannot resume sending. A second re-key before the first one
26:  took over replaces the waiting next generation.
27:- Receive locators name exactly one generation of a peer, so a locator already in use by a peer's current, next or
28:  prev generation is refused (`-EEXIST`).
29:- A transmit that read the current generation just before a switch looks again once, instead of being dropped.
30:
31:The same rule applies on both sides, with no new message and no change to the wire, the Netlink ABI or the
32:controller. Whichever side finishes first keeps sending on the old keys until the other proves it has the new
33:ones, or the 2 seconds are up, so neither side sends keys the other cannot read.
